population.definition: Census 2017 (RGPH-2017) count for the administrative subdivision 'Moroni Bambao' on Ngazidja (61,867 male, 59,369 female). This is a subdivision, not a strict city or agglomeration count; the table does not say which localities it includes. The census manual lists Moroni among 'urban' localities. EBSCO gives a different, non-census figure (about 90,400, World Population Review estimate) without a definition.

source.title: Principaux indicateurs du Recensement general de la population et de l'habitat de 2017 en Union des Comores (RGPH-2017)
source.publisher: INSEED (Institut national de la statistique et des etudes economiques et demographiques), Comoros
source.quote: Moroni Bambao 121 236 (total), 61 867 masculin, 59 369 feminin

facts.claim: Moroni became the administrative capital of the Comoros; sources differ on the year the colonial capital moved there (1958 per EBSCO's full article, 1962 per Library of Congress) and EBSCO also ties it to independence in 1975.

source.title: Comoros - The Issue of Mahore
source.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress (Comoros: A Country Study), hosted at countrystudies.us
source.quote: the colonial capital was moved from the Mahore town of Dzaoudzi to Moroni on Njazidja in 1962

facts.claim: Protectorate treaties were signed with the rulers of Njazidja, Nzwani and Mwali in 1886; the islands joined France's Madagascar colony in 1908 and the last sultan abdicated in 1912.

source.title: Comoros - French Colonization
source.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress (Comoros: A Country Study), hosted at countrystudies.us
source.quote: with the rulers of Njazidja, Nzwani, and Mwali in 1886

facts.claim: Independence was declared on 6 July 1975 by the Comorian government for all the islands including Mayotte (Mahore); the Mayotte status remains disputed, with the Comorian position stated in UN debates.

source.title: Comoros - The Issue of Mahore
source.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress (Comoros: A Country Study), hosted at countrystudies.us
source.quote: declaring independence unilaterally on July 6, 1975, for all Comoro Islands, including Mahore

facts.claim: In a 1976 UN General Assembly debate on 'Question of the Comorian island of Mayotte', Mauritius's delegate stated the Comorian-sovereignty position (attributed statement, one delegate; page is a third-party OCR transcript of the UN record A/31/PV.38, 20 October 1976).

source.title: A/31/PV.38 General Assembly, Session 31, Meeting 38
source.publisher: UN Project (transcription of UN General Assembly record)
source.author: Mr. Ramphul (Mauritius), speaker
source.quote: Mayotte is an integral part of the State of Comoros.
